Inflation is a sustained increase in the general price level of goods and services. Consider, for a moment, what that really means, because it is easy to hear a word like this so often that it stops meaning anything at all, and it is worth slowing down to sit with it properly. When prices rise generally, a unit of currency purchases fewer goods and services, and so the same money that once carried you a certain distance now carries you a little less far, quietly, without announcing itself, week after week, in ways that are easy to miss until they are not. That is the whole of it, and yet it touches almost everything people do with money, which is why it deserves careful, patient attention rather than a quick glance.
